chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Many a man faces a day after which he finds no day and many a man is in an enviable position in the earlier part of the night but is wept over by bewailing women in its later part.

key_terms.بَوَاكِيهِ: The women who wail/mourn over him
key_terms.مَغْبُوطٍ: One who is envied or considered fortunate
key_terms.مُسْتَدْبِرِهِ: His back is turned to it; he no longer experiences it
key_terms.مُسْتَقْبِلٍ: One who faces or looks forward to a future time

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'faces a day after which he finds no day' mean in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the unpredictability of divine decree by contrasting the envied status of the morning with the weeping mourners of the evening, a metaphor for life's sudden transitions. This hadith, found in the *Nahj al-Balagha*, serves as a profound reminder of *al-fana'* (impermanence) and the fragility of worldly power, urging believers to maintain humility and spiritual readiness for the inevitable shift from joy to sorrow.
